facts.fact: The E. Clarke and Julia Arnold House is a Usonian home designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in Columbus, Wisconsin.
facts.quote: The E. Clarke and Julia Arnold House is a Frank Lloyd Wright designed Usonian home in Columbus, Wisconsin, United States.

facts.fact: It sits on a large site on the west edge of Columbus, looking over farmland, and was built in 1955–1956 for the attorney E. Clarke Arnold and his family.
facts.quote: The Arnold house occupies a large site on the west edge of the city of Columbus and overlooks the farmlands to the west. It was built in 1955-1956 for E. Clarke Arnold, a successful Columbus attorney, his wife, Julia, and their growing family, from a design supplied by Frank Lloyd Wright.

facts.fact: The low one-storey house is built of Wisconsin limestone, redwood board and batten, and glass.
facts.quote: This low one-story home is built of Wisconsin limestone, redwood board and batten, and glass.

facts.fact: It is one of Wright's diamond-module houses: every angle is 60° or 120°, forming parallelogram modules with 4-foot sides.
facts.quote: In this design, all the angles are either 60°or 120°, forming equilateral parallelogram modules having 4-foot-long (1.2 m) sides.

facts.fact: It was first built as a V-shaped plan: a living-room wing and a bedroom wing set at 120°, with a central core holding the fireplace, kitchen and utilities.
facts.quote: It was originally built with two wings set at 120° angles which gave the house a V-shaped plan with a living room wing, a bedroom wing, and a central core that contained the fireplace mass, kitchen, and utilities.

facts.fact: Instead of Wright's usual Cherokee Red, the floors are golden ochre.
facts.quote: This home featured a twist on the usual Usonian color scheme with Golden ocher floors instead of the signature "Cherokee Red."

facts.fact: Wright's apprentice John H. Howe drafted a revised design for a second wing, which gave the house its final Y-shaped plan.
facts.quote: Wright apprentice and Taliesin Fellow John H. "Jack" Howe drafted a second, partly revised design, which established the final Y-shaped plan of the house.

facts.fact: Eden Court is a large theatre, cinema and arts venue in Inverness, close to the banks of the River Ness.
facts.quote: Eden Court Theatre (Scottish Gaelic: Cùirt an Easbaig, "Bishop's Court") is a large theatre, cinema and arts venue situated in Inverness, Scotland close to the banks of the River Ness.

facts.fact: It opened on 15 April 1976.
facts.quote: The Eden Court Theatre was formally opened on 15 April 1976 by Andrew Cruickshank MBE, an actor best known for his portrayal of Dr Cameron in BBC's long-running series "Dr Finlay's Casebook".

facts.fact: The new building by Law Dunbar and Naismith took in the Gothic Bishop's Palace, which gave the theatre its name.
facts.quote: It was built on a site next to the Ness river, and incorporated the Gothic Bishop's Palace residence (from which it took its name) into a new building designed by architects Law Dunbar and Naismith.

facts.fact: It gave Inverness modern theatre space for the first time since the early 1930s.
facts.quote: It provided modern theatre performance space for the first time since the early 1930s.

facts.fact: It reopened in November 2007 after a full refurbishment and extension with Page\Park Architects, becoming Scotland's largest combined arts centre.
facts.quote: Eden Court reopened in November 2007, having undergone a complete refurbishment and extension by Robertson Construction and Page\Park Architects.  Upon its reopening it became the largest combined arts centre in Scotland.

facts.fact: The extension added a second theatre, two cinema screens and two performance and dance studios.
facts.quote: The theatre has recently undergone a complete refurbishment and major extension, adding a second theatre, two dedicated cinema screens, two performance/dance studios, improved dressing room and green room facilities and additional office space.

facts.fact: The main auditorium seats just under 840 and the second about 270.
facts.quote: The main auditorium, renamed the Empire Theatre, has a capacity of just under 840.  The second auditorium, named the OneTouch Theatre, has a capacity of about 270.

facts.fact: The carpentry work in the Bishop's Palace won the 2009 Specialist Carpentry Refurbishment Award.
facts.quote: It won the 2009 "Specialist Carpentry Refurbishment Award" for the high standard of carpentry work carried out in the Bishop's Palace as undertaken by specialist contractor Ryvoan Developments.

facts.fact: Alejandro de la Sota's works include the Gobierno Civil in Tarragona, 1956–1963.
facts.quote: Gobierno Civil (Tarragona) (1956-1963)

facts.fact: De la Sota promoted the industrialisation of construction in the 1960s.
facts.quote: He was a promoter of the industrialisation of construction in the 1960s.

facts.fact: Hamilton City Hall is the city's chief administrative building, an 8-storey (34 m) block downtown at Main Street West and Bay Street South.
facts.quote: Located in the downtown core, it is an 8-storey building (34.0 m) at the corner of Main Street West and Bay Street South, across the street from the FirstOntario Concert Hall and the Art Gallery of Hamilton.

facts.fact: It opened on 21 November 1960.
facts.quote: It was officially opened on November 21, 1960.

facts.fact: It was designed by Stanley Roscoe in the International Style.
facts.quote: This international style of architecture was designed by architect Stanley Roscoe.

facts.fact: It cost 9.4 million dollars to build.
facts.quote: Construction was carried out by the Pigott Construction Company, at a cost of 9.4 million dollars.

facts.fact: Its address, 71 Main Street West, marks the 71 years the old City Hall had been in use.
facts.quote: They chose 71 to commemorate the number of years that the old City Hall on James Street North had been in use.

facts.fact: The city designated it a heritage building in 2005; its Italian glass tile mosaics are among the protected features.
facts.quote: In 2005, Hamilton City Council designated the building as a heritage structure. Among the listed heritage elements on the exterior are the Italian glass tile mosaics.

facts.fact: The council ordered a renovation in May 2007, and the project's launch phase began in June 2008.
facts.quote: In May 2007, Hamilton City Council directed staff to proceed with the renovation of the building, and the launch phase of the project began in June 2008.

facts.fact: The Kreeger Museum, on Foxhall Road in Washington, D.C., is the former home of Carmen and David Lloyd Kreeger and holds their art collection.
facts.quote: It is located on Foxhall Road, one of the residential neighborhoods of the city, in the former home of Carmen and David Lloyd Kreeger and it contains the art collection of nineteenth- and twentieth-century paintings and sculpture they acquired from 1952 to 1988.

facts.fact: The brief was a private house that would one day become a museum; it was the Kreegers' home from 1967 to 1990.
facts.quote: The design brief was for a private residence that, one day, would become a museum harbouring the art collection acquired by the Kreegers. The building served as the Kreeger home from 1967 to 1990.

facts.fact: Philip Johnson proposed a modern Roman villa, with sculpture terraces, reflecting pools and indoor and outdoor gardens.
facts.quote: Johnson proposed a modern interpretation of a Roman villa, complete with sculpture terraces and reflecting pools, set in a décor of sprawling indoor and outdoor gardens.

facts.fact: The house is a set of asymmetrically arranged, groin-vaulted cubes: travertine walls face the street and glass walls open to the woods.
facts.quote: For the Kreeger residence, Johnson envisaged a composition of asymmetrically arranged, groin-vaulted cubes with travertine walls facing the street and glass walls that open up vistas onto the wooded site surrounding the house.

facts.fact: The plan is built on a module of 22 x 22 x 22 ft cubes, which can serve as living space, gallery or both.
facts.quote: The building with a gross surface area of 24,000 ft2 (2230 m2) was designed on the basis of a modular system of cubes measuring 22 x 22 x 22 ft (6,7 x 6,7 x 6,7 m). The modular concept allowed the cubes to be adapted for different functions : living space, gallery space or both.

facts.fact: The two-storey Great Hall rises to 25 feet under three vaulted domes, whose shape gives it acoustics suited to chamber and piano music.
facts.quote: The largest open space in the building, The Great Hall, a two-story space that rises up to 25 feet (7,6 m), is topped by 3 vaulted domes that create a natural amplification system and provides acoustics suitable for chamber and piano music.

facts.fact: Seventeen concrete domes form the roof.
facts.quote: Seventeen concrete domes form the distinctive roof and are covered with a synthetic rubberized waterproofing material.

facts.fact: The exterior is clad in 900 tonnes of hand-selected Italian travertine.
facts.quote: The modern exterior, inspired in part by Philip Johnson's admiration for and prior collaboration with Ludwig Mies van der Rohe on the Seagram Building in New York, is clad with 900 tonnes of hand-selected Italian travertine slabs.

facts.fact: The Marisfrolg Pavilion in Longhua District, Shenzhen, is the headquarters of the fashion brand Marisfrolg.
facts.quote: Marisfrolg Pavilion (simplified Chinese: 玛丝菲尔大厦; traditional Chinese: 瑪絲菲爾大廈), located in Longhua District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, China, is the headquarters of the Shenzhen fashion brand Marisfrolg.

facts.fact: Designed by the New Zealand studio Architecture Van Brandenburg, its forms are inspired by tropical plants and the spiky exoskeletons of insects.
facts.quote: Designed by New Zealand Studio Architecture Van Brandenburg (AVB), the building features biomimetic designs inspired by tropical plants and the spiky exoskeletons of insects.

facts.fact: The structure combines steel and reinforced concrete, and the outside is a mosaic of tiles, brick fragments and stones.
facts.quote: The main structure is a combination of steel and reinforced concrete, with the exterior decorated using a mosaic of tiles, brick fragments, and stones.

facts.fact: It stands on an island site of 5.5 hectares.
facts.quote: The building is on an island site of 5.5 hectares with a 120,000-square-metre.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2008 and took 15 years.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2008 and took 15 years to complete.

facts.fact: Its architecture seems influenced by early Gaudí and by Santiago Calatrava, and it drew attention at the 14th Venice Biennale of Architecture.
facts.quote: The architecture seems to have been influenced by the early style of Antoni Gaudí and Santiago Calatrava. It had received attention at the 14th Venice Biennale of Architecture.

facts.fact: The museum opened in 2000 in the Batō area of Nakagawa, Tochigi Prefecture.
facts.quote: Nakagawa-machi Batō Hiroshige Museum of Art (那珂川町馬頭広重美術館, Nakagawa-machi Batō Hiroshige Bijutsukan) opened in the Batō area of Nakagawa, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan, in 2000.

facts.fact: Its prize-winning building is by Kengo Kuma, and it holds paintings by Hiroshige and woodblock prints of the Utagawa school.
facts.quote: In a prize-winning building designed by Kuma Kengo, the museum's collection includes nikuhitsu-ga by Hiroshige, woodblock prints of the Utagawa school, Meiji-period prints by Kobayashi Kiyochika, and works by Kawamura Kiyoo.

facts.fact: Kuma won the 2001 Togo Murano Award for the museum.
facts.quote: 2001 Togo Murano Award for “Nakagawa-machi Bato Hiroshige Museum”

facts.fact: Jean Nouvel's notable works include the Palais de Justice in Nantes, 2000.
facts.quote: 2000 – Palais de Justice, Nantes, France

facts.fact: The Pritzker Prize named the Nantes courthouse among Nouvel's major works in Europe.
facts.quote: Pritzker points to several more major works: in Europe, the Cartier Foundation for Contemporary Art (1994), the Culture and Convention Center in Lucerne (2000), the Opéra Nouvel in Lyon (1993), Expo 2002 in Switzerland and, under construction, the Copenhagen Concert Hall and the courthouse in Nantes (2000); as well as two tall towers in planning in North America, Tour Verre in New York City and a cancelled condominium tower in Los Angeles.

facts.fact: The museum was created in 2008 from the former Narayanhiti Palace, after the 2006 revolution.
facts.quote: The museum was created in 2008 from the complex of the former Narayanhiti Palace (or Narayanhiti Durbar) following the 2006 revolution.

facts.fact: Before the revolution the palace was the home and main workplace of Nepal's king and hosted state occasions.
facts.quote: Before the revolution, the palace was the residence and principal workplace of the monarch of the Kingdom of Nepal, and hosted occasions of state.

facts.fact: King Mahendra had the old palace replaced in 1963; the new one was designed by the American architect Benjamin Polk, who lived in India.
facts.quote: King Mahendra ordered the palace to be demolished and replaced in 1963. The new palace was designed by American architect Benjamin Polk, who was living in India.

facts.fact: Nepalese architectural styles were used to make it a national symbol; construction ended in 1969.
facts.quote: Nepalese architecture styles were used to create a national symbol. Construction ended in 1969.

facts.fact: Its iconic central tower rises above the front of the palace as an extension of the Hindu temple beneath it.
facts.quote: This is the iconic central tower that rises above the palace in the front. The tower is an extension of the Hindu temple beneath it.

facts.fact: The palace covers 3,794 m² in three parts: a guest wing, a state wing and a private wing.
facts.quote: The Palace stands on the floor space of  3,794 m2 (40838.28 sq ft) and is divided into three parts, the guest wing, the state wing and the private wing.

facts.fact: The throne room follows Hindu temple architecture, with a 48-foot chandelier under a 60-foot pagoda-style ceiling on four concrete columns.
facts.quote: Construction of Gorkha Baithak is based on Hindu temple architect style with a 48-foot chandelier hanging on a 60-foot high Pagoda style ceiling standing on four concrete columns representing Nāga and decorated with Hindu guardian demigods the Astha Matrikas and Ashta Bhairava.

facts.fact: The Nilson Nelson Gymnasium is an indoor arena in Brasília, used mostly for volleyball, next to the Mané Garrincha stadium.
facts.quote: The Nilson Nelson Gymnasium (Ginásio Nilson Nelson) is an indoor sporting arena used mostly for volleyball located in Brasília, Brazil, which is near the Estádio Nacional Mané Garrincha.

facts.fact: It is part of the Ayrton Senna Sports Complex.
facts.quote: Both are part of the Ayrton Senna Sports Complex.

facts.fact: It was designed by Cláudio Cianciarullo and opened on 21 April 1973.
facts.quote: The hall was designed by Cláudio Cianciarullo and opened on April 21, 1973.

facts.fact: It held 24,286 people until a 2008 renovation cut its capacity to 11,105.
facts.quote: From 1973 to 2008, the arena had a capacity of 24,286 seats. In 2008, the multi-purpose arena was renovated and reduced the spectator capacity to 11,105 seats.

facts.fact: It is used mainly for indoor sports and was a venue of the 2008 FIFA Futsal World Cup.
facts.quote: It is used mainly for indoor sports, and was the secondary venue at 2008 FIFA Futsal World Cup.

facts.fact: The Otaniemi Chapel was built in 1957, by the same architects as the first student houses of Teekkarikylä.
facts.quote: The Otaniemi Chapel, designed by the same architects, was built 1957.

facts.fact: The chapel is noted for balancing Finnish rural architecture with a modernism influenced by Alvar Aalto's red-brick period of the 1950s.
facts.quote: The Otaniemi Chapel is noted for its delicate balance between features of Finnish rural architecture and a modernism, influenced by Alvar Aalto's redbrick period of the 1950s.

facts.fact: Kaija Siren designed most of her works with her husband, Heikki Siren.
facts.quote: Siren designed most of her works together with her spouse, the prominent Finnish architect Heikki Siren.

facts.fact: The Palau Sant Jordi is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Barcelona's Olympic Ring.
facts.quote: The Palau Sant Jordi (Catalan pronunciation: [pəˈlaw ˈsaɲ ˈʒɔɾði], English: St. George's Palace) is a multi-purpose indoor arena that is part of the Olympic Ring complex located in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

facts.fact: It was designed by Arata Isozaki and opened in 1990; with up to 17,960 seats it is Spain's largest indoor arena.
facts.quote: Designed by the Japanese architect Arata Isozaki, it was opened in 1990. With a maximum seating capacity of 17,960, it is the largest indoor arena in Spain.

facts.fact: It was one of the main venues of the 1992 Summer Olympics, for gymnastics, handball and volleyball.
facts.quote: The Palau Sant Jordi was one of the main venues of the 1992 Summer Olympics, hosting the artistic gymnastics, handball, and volleyball events.

facts.fact: Its flexibility lets it host sport, concerts and other cultural events.
facts.quote: Today, it is used for a variety of indoor sport events as well as for concerts and other cultural activities, due to its great flexibility.

facts.fact: It was the main venue of the FINA World Championships, with a temporary regulation swimming pool installed.
facts.quote: Palau Sant Jordi was the main venue of the FINA World Championships. A temporary, regulation swimming pool was installed for the occasion.

facts.fact: Isozaki worked on it from 1983 to 1990.
facts.quote: Palau Sant Jordi main indoor venue during the 1992 Summer Olympics, (1983–1990) Barcelona, Spain

facts.fact: The Savill Building, a visitor centre designed by Glenn Howells Architects, opened in June 2006.
facts.quote: In June 2006, a specially designed new visitor centre, the Savill Building by Glenn Howells Architects was opened.

facts.fact: It was shortlisted for the 2007 RIBA Stirling Prize.
facts.quote: Among its public projects is the Savill Building at Windsor Great Park, shortlisted for the 2007 RIBA Stirling Prize.

facts.fact: It won a Crown Estate competition for a gateway to the listed gardens that reflects the park's character.
facts.quote: The competition winning scheme run by The Crown Estate, was intended to create a gateway to the listed gardens reflecting the character and quality of the park.

facts.fact: All visitor facilities sit under one gridshell roof, forming a series of linked spaces.
facts.quote: The building grouped all visitor facilities under a grid shell roof creating a series of linked spaces.

facts.fact: The roof is built of larch and clad in green oak from sustainable sources on the Windsor Estate.
facts.quote: The roof is constructed from larch and clad with green oak from sustainable sources from the Windsor Estate.

facts.fact: An earth bank on the entrance side holds the ancillary rooms, while the garden side stands on legs to make the most of the views.
facts.quote: It is supported by an earth structure on the entrance side which houses ancillary facilities, while the garden side is elevated on legs to take advantage of the views.

facts.fact: The timber for the floor and roof came from the Windsor Estate.
facts.quote: The timber for the floor and roof came from the Windsor Estate.

facts.fact: The Transportation Center Skopje is the city's main railway station and bus terminal.
facts.quote: The Transportation Center Skopje, or Skopje railway station (Macedonian: Транспортен центар Скопје; Albanian: Qendra transportuese e Shkupit  / Macedonian: Железничка станица Скопје; Albanian: Stacioni hekurudhor i Shkupit) is the main central passenger railway station and bus terminal in the Republic of North Macedonia capital Skopje.

facts.fact: It was built after the 1963 earthquake destroyed the original station and much of the city.
facts.quote: It was built after the 1963 Skopje earthquake that destroyed the original station buildings, and much of the city.

facts.fact: Its 10 tracks sit on a massive concrete bridge 2 km long.
facts.quote: There are 10 tracks placed on a massive concrete bridge 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) long.

facts.fact: After the earthquake Kenzō Tange drew up a plan to rebuild the city, never fully carried out.
facts.quote: After the earthquake, a project was started for a major reconstruction of the city, authored by Kenzo Tange, a Japanese architect, but which has not been fully implemented.

facts.fact: The station was rebuilt in the Brutalist style and completed in 1981.
facts.quote: The station was rebuilt in the Brutalist style of architecture. It was completed in 1981.

facts.fact: It stands on earthquake-proof concrete pillars under a tubular platform hall.
facts.quote: The construction is supported by earthquake-proof concrete pillars and covered by a tubular platform hall.

facts.fact: Ticket counters and waiting rooms sit below the platforms behind glass façades, with exposed concrete walls and ceilings inside.
facts.quote: Below the platforms are the counter and waiting rooms, which are separated from the street by glass facades. The interiors are designed with exposed concrete walls and ceilings in the Brutalist style.

facts.fact: The old station, its clock stopped at 5.17, is now the Museum of the City of Skopje.
facts.quote: The old station building has become a symbol of the earthquake, with the clock stopped at 5.17 and now houses the Museum of the City of Skopje (Muzej na grad Skopje).

facts.fact: The Taipei Fine Arts Museum is in Taipei Expo Park.
facts.quote: It is in the Taipei Expo Park.

facts.fact: It opened on 8 August 1983 on the former site of the United States Taiwan Defense Command.
facts.quote: The museum first opened on August 8, 1983, at the former site of the United States Taiwan Defense Command.

facts.fact: It was the first museum in Taiwan built for contemporary art exhibitions.
facts.quote: It was the first museum in Taiwan built for contemporary art exhibitions.

facts.fact: Its architecture, by Kao Er-pan, is a local interpretation of Japanese Metabolism.
facts.quote: The architecture is a local interpretation of the Japanese Metabolist Movement, and the building was designed by architect Kao Er-Pan.

facts.fact: The city decided to build a high-standard museum in 1976.
facts.quote: In 1976, following the central government's decision enhance the cultural life of city, the Taipei Municipal Government embarked on a plan to build a high-standard museum.

facts.fact: It hosts the Taipei Biennial; the 1996 edition used all floors of the building.
facts.quote: In 1996 the largest ever Taipei Biennial was held under the title "The Quest for Identity", involving 110 artists and all floors of the building.

facts.fact: The Teien Art Museum is in Shirokanedai, Tokyo, just east of Meguro Station.
facts.quote: The museum is located in Minato ward, just east of Meguro Station.

facts.fact: The Art Deco building, completed in 1933, has interiors by Henri Rapin and glass by René Lalique.
facts.quote: The Art Deco building, completed in 1933, has interiors designed by Henri Rapin and features decorative glass work by René Lalique.

facts.fact: It was the home of Prince Asaka Yasuhiko and his family from 1933 to 1947.
facts.quote: The Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum building was the residence of Prince Asaka Yasuhiko and his family from 1933 to 1947.

facts.fact: Henri Rapin planned many of the interiors, but the building's main architect is credited as Gondo Yukichi of the Imperial Household Ministry's Works Bureau.
facts.quote: Although many of the interiors were designed according to plans submitted by Henri Rapin, the main architect of the building itself is credited as Gondo Yukichi of the Works Bureau of the Imperial Household Ministry.

facts.fact: After the war it was the Prime Minister's residence and then a State Guest House, and it opened as a museum in 1983.
facts.quote: After World War II the building served as the official residence of the Prime Minister (1947–50), and as a State Guest House (1950–74). The residence was first opened to the public as a museum in 1983.

facts.fact: It is named teien, Japanese garden, because gardens and sculptures surround it.
facts.quote: Teien means Japanese garden, and the museum is so named because the building is surrounded by a garden and sculptures.

facts.fact: After a renovation begun in 2013 it reopened in November 2014, with a new annex designed with Hiroshi Sugimoto.
facts.quote: After undergoing extensive renovation in 2013, the museum was re-opened in November 2014. The new museum annex, designed in collaboration with Hiroshi Sugimoto includes modern exhibition spaces, a café and museum shop.

facts.fact: Designed by Viljo Revell and engineered by Hannskarl Bandel, the Neo-Expressionist hall opened in 1965 together with Nathan Phillips Square in front of it.
facts.quote: Designed by Viljo Revell and engineered by Hannskarl Bandel, this example of Neo-Expressionist Modern architecture opened in 1965. Adjacent is the Nathan Phillips Square public square, designed and opened together with the hall.

facts.fact: The hall and square came from a 1958 international competition, the first in Ontario open to foreign architects.
facts.quote: It was the first architectural competition in Ontario to allow international architects, requiring the local architects' association to change its rules and allow open competition at the instigation of then Toronto Mayor Nathan Phillips, after whom the square is named.

facts.fact: Revell's entry was first discarded, until juror Eero Saarinen picked it out and convinced the others to reconsider it.
facts.quote: He chose Revell's design and convinced the other judges to reconsider it.

facts.fact: Two curved towers of different heights surround a saucer-shaped council chamber on a two-storey podium.
facts.quote: The design is two curved, asymmetric towers surrounding a saucer-shaped council chamber amphitheatre atop a two-storey podium.

facts.fact: The east tower is 27 storeys and the west tower 20, built of poured concrete.
facts.quote: The east tower is 27 storeys (99.5 metres [326 ft]) tall and the west tower is 20 storeys (79.4 metres [260 ft]). The structure is constructed of poured concrete.

facts.fact: The windowless backs of the towers are clad in 4,000 ribbed concave concrete panels inlaid with Botticino marble, so the towers would sparkle when floodlit.
facts.quote: The towers have windowless back walls, which are clad in preclad ribbed concave concrete panels with inlaid strips of Botticino marble. Revell designed the 4,000 panels' mixed construction so that the towers would "sparkle when floodlit."

facts.fact: The council chamber is covered by a shallow dome resting on 23 pairs of V-shaped supports.
facts.quote: The room is covered by a shallow dome resting on 23 pairs of v-shaped supports that rise from the base.

facts.fact: The city designated it a property of historical and architectural significance in 1991.
facts.quote: City Hall was designated as a property of historical and architectural significance under the Ontario Heritage Act in 1991 by Toronto City Council.

facts.fact: The Torre Latinoamericana is a 166 m skyscraper in downtown Mexico City and one of the city's key landmarks.
facts.quote: Its central location, height (166 m; 545 ft),  and history make it one of the city's most important landmarks.

facts.fact: From its opening in 1956 until 1982 it was Mexico's tallest completed building.
facts.quote: The Torre Latinoamericana was Mexico's tallest completed building for almost 27 years,  from its opening in 1956 until 1982 when the 214 m (702 ft) tall Torre Ejecutiva Pemex was completed.

facts.fact: It was built as the headquarters of the insurance company La Latinoamericana, Seguros.
facts.quote: The Torre Latinoamericana was built to headquarter La Latinoamericana, Seguros, S.A., an insurance company founded on April 30, 1906.

facts.fact: A steel frame and deep piles were needed for Mexico City's frequent earthquakes and soft, muddy soil.
facts.quote: Its design consists of a steel-frame construction and deep-seated piles, which were necessary given Mexico City's frequent earthquakes and muddy soil composition, which makes the terrain tricky to build on.

facts.fact: Its engineers studied the site's soil before designing the structure, an innovation at the time.
facts.quote: Before construction, both engineers carried out a number of soil mechanics studies in the construction site, and designed the structure accordingly. Today this is common and even mandatory practice, but at the time it was quite an innovation.

facts.fact: It withstood the magnitude 8.1 earthquake of 1985 without damage, while several other downtown buildings were damaged.
facts.quote: The skyscraper notably withstood the 8.1 magnitude 1985 Mexico City earthquake without damage, whereas several other structures in the downtown area were damaged.

facts.fact: Its observation deck on the 44th floor is the highest in Mexico City.
facts.quote: Its public observation deck on the 44th floor is the highest in Mexico City.

facts.fact: Its architect Augusto H. Álvarez was influenced by the International Style of Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe.
facts.quote: His design works were influenced by the International style architecture of Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe.

facts.fact: First built as a school for orphans, it now houses several cultural institutions.
facts.quote: Originally built as a learning center for orphans, it currently hosts several cultural institutions.

facts.fact: Built by the Ministry of Labour from 1946 to 1955, it covers 270,000 m², the largest building in Spain, bigger than El Escorial.
facts.quote: Built between 1946 and 1955 by the Ministry of Labour, it is considered the most important architectural work built in the 20th century in Asturias and, with its 270,000 m2, the largest building in Spain, even larger than the Monastery of El Escorial.

facts.fact: It was built to educate orphans of men killed working in the mines.
facts.quote: The building was originally built to educate orphans whose parents had died as a result of working in the mining industry.

facts.fact: Luis Moya modelled it on the Parthenon and turned the main gate away from the city, so visitors walk around it before entering.
facts.quote: Luis Moya, who designed the facility along the lines of the Parthenon in Athens, chose to have the main gate face away from the city, so that visitors coming from Gijón would have to walk around the university before entering, and therefore fully admire its magnificence.

facts.fact: The whole building is organised around a roofless courtyard of 150 by 50 m.
facts.quote: The roofless courtyard with an area of 150×50 m2. The entire building is structured around the courtyard.

facts.fact: The church's dome weighs 2,300 tons and rises 32 m above the floor.
facts.quote: The church has a 2,300-ton dome. The height between the floor and the highest point of the dome is 32 m.

facts.fact: Its tower is the tallest building in Asturias and the tallest stone building in Spain.
facts.quote: The tower of the Universidad Laboral is the tallest building in Asturias and the tallest stone building in Spain.

facts.fact: Abandoned in the 1980s, the whole building was restored between 2001 and 2007.
facts.quote: Abandoned in the 1980s, the whole building was restored between 2001 and 2007.

facts.fact: Built between 1906 and 1921 under the British Raj, it is dedicated to the memory of Queen Victoria.
facts.quote: It was built between 1906 and 1921 by the British Raj. It is dedicated to the memory of Queen Victoria, the Empress of India from 1876 to 1901.

facts.fact: Its architect was William Emerson, and its style is Indo-Saracenic, mixing British and Mughal elements with Venetian, Egyptian and Deccani influences.
facts.quote: The architect of the Victoria Memorial was William Emerson (1843–1924). The design is in the Indo-Saracenic style, mixing British and Mughal elements with Venetian, Egyptian, and Deccani architectural influences.

facts.fact: The building is 338 by 228 ft, rises to 184 ft, and is built of white Makrana marble.
facts.quote: The building is 338 by 228 ft (103 by 69 m) and rises to a height of 184 ft (56 m). It is constructed of white Makrana marble.

facts.fact: Curzon made the central chamber 64 ft across so it would be slightly larger than the Taj Mahal's.
facts.quote: Curzon deliberately intended the central chamber to be 64 ft (20 m) in diameter in order to be slightly larger than the Taj Mahal.

facts.fact: It echoes the Taj Mahal with its dome, four subsidiary domes, chhatris, high portals, terrace and domed corner towers.
facts.quote: In design it echoes the Taj Mahal with its dome, four subsidiaries, octagonal-domed chattris, high portals, terrace, and domed corner towers.

facts.fact: 78 Derngate is a Grade II* listed Georgian house of 1815 in Northampton.

facts.fact: Doha Tower is a 238-metre, 46-storey office building designed by Jean Nouvel.
facts.quote: The $125-million office building, designed by French architect Jean Nouvel, has a height of 238 metres (781 ft), with 46 stories.

facts.fact: It has no central core, leaving more internal space for occupants.
facts.quote: It has no central core, leaving more internal space available to its occupants.

facts.fact: It was the first skyscraper with internal reinforced concrete diagrid columns, forming a cross shape tied to the cylindrical facade.
facts.quote: The design is unique, the first skyscraper with internal reinforced concrete diagrid columns, which form a cross (X) shape that connects with the eye-catching cylindrical facade.

facts.fact: Its screens draw on Islamic mashrabiya and shade the building from heat and sand.
facts.quote: Islamic screens were designed to shade the building from high temperatures as well as the unpleasant sand residue found on glass throughout the region.

facts.fact: Its cylinder recalls Nouvel's Torre Glòries in Barcelona, which inspired it.
facts.quote: Its cylindrical shape is reminiscent of Nouvel's Torre Glòries office building in Barcelona, which served as conceptual inspiration for the Doha Tower.

facts.fact: The cylinder is 45 metres across at the base and crowned by a dome.
facts.quote: The pinnacle of the cylindrical building, which has a base of 45 metres (148 ft) in diameter, is crowned by a dome.

facts.fact: In 2012 it won the CTBUH award for Best Tall Building Worldwide.
facts.quote: On October 18, 2012, the building received the CTBUH Skyscraper Award for the Best Tall Building Worldwide from the CTBUH.

facts.fact: Dokk1 is a public library, culture centre and municipal building on the Aarhus waterfront.
facts.quote: Dokk1 or Dokken is a government building, public library and culture center in Aarhus, Denmark.

facts.fact: It was designed by Schmidt Hammer Lassen Architects and Kristine Jensen and opened on 20 June 2015.
facts.quote: It is designed by Schmidt Hammer Lassen Architects and Kristine Jensen, with construction managed by NCC AB. Construction broke ground 8 June 2011 and the building was inaugurated four years later on 20 June 2015.

facts.fact: The building is a seven-sided metal disc floating above a glass prism that rests on wide irregular stairs on all sides.
facts.quote: The neo-futuristic building is designed as a heptagonal metal disc floating above a glass prism which rests on a bed of wide irregular staircases to all sides.

facts.fact: The disc holds offices, while the transparent glass prism holds the library, open to views of harbour, bay, forest and city.
facts.quote: The metal disc holds offices and administration while the glass prism houses the public library, designed to be transparent to all sides and making all activities within visible from the outside, while providing a view across the harbour, bay, forest and city from within.

facts.fact: Light rail trains run through and under the building, which includes a station.
facts.quote: The structure is integrated with the light rail system with trains running through and under the building including a station.

facts.fact: A 2,432 m² solar array is on the roof and seawater is used for cooling.
facts.quote: Among the many initiatives, a 2,432 m2 (26,180 sq ft) solar panel has been added to the roof, seawater is used as a coolant for both excessive heat and ventilation and LED lights are used extensively.

facts.fact: A bronze bell by Kirstine Roepstorff hangs over the central stair and rings when babies are born at the city hospital.
facts.quote: The bell is connected to the Aarhus University Hospital where parents can push a button to activate it when their newborns have been successfully delivered.

facts.fact: In 2016 it was named Public Library of the Year by IFLA.
facts.quote: In 2016, Dokk1 was named Public Library of the Year by the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions.

facts.fact: Demas Nwoko's first major architectural design was for a Dominican mission in Ibadan.
facts.quote: Nwoko's first major architectural design was for a Dominican mission in Ibadan.

facts.fact: Asked first to design a plaque for a new chapel, Nwoko asked the Dominican fathers to let him design the chapel itself.
facts.quote: He was originally approached to design a plaque for a new chapel but he later asked the Dominican fathers to help in designing a new chapel to be located in Ibadan.

facts.fact: His freehand design was made to suit local conditions such as Ibadan's strong sun.
facts.quote: Although, his initial design was a little bit crude with the utilisation of free-hand drawing, it was meant to accommodate local exigencies such as the sunny atmosphere in Ibadan.

facts.fact: Nwoko designed his buildings to keep interior temperatures unlike those outside.
facts.quote: Usually, his designs were designed to have interior temperatures to be in contrast to the exterior temperatures at most times.

facts.fact: His work, including the Dominican Institute in Ibadan, fuses modern techniques with African tradition.
facts.quote: Nwoko's works fuse modern techniques in architecture and stage design with African tradition.

facts.fact: The Avianca Building is a 161-metre office skyscraper beside Santander Park in Bogotá.
facts.quote: Avianca Building is a 161-meter-tall office skyscraper located at the intersection of 16th street and Seventh Avenue, next to Santander Park in the city of Bogotá, Colombia.

facts.fact: Esguerra, Sáenz, Urdaneta, Samper y Cía. designed and built it with Ricaurte Prieto Carrizosa and engineer Doménico Parma, after a competition.
facts.quote: The Avianca Building was designed and constructed by Esguerra, Sáenz, Urdaneta, Samper y Cía., together with Ricaurte Prieto Carrizosa and Italian engineer Doménico Parma, after a competition among several of the most prominent architectural firms in Colombia.

facts.fact: The design was finished in 1963 and it was built from 1966 to 1969 on the site of the Hotel Regina.
facts.quote: The design was completed in 1963, and construction took place between 1966 and 1969 on the former site of the demolished Hotel Regina.

facts.fact: It opened at the end of 1969 as the headquarters of the airline Avianca.
facts.quote: The building was inaugurated at the end of 1969 as the headquarters of the airline Avianca.

facts.fact: On completion it was the tallest building in Colombia.
facts.quote: Upon its completion, the Avianca Building became the tallest building in Bogotá and Colombia, and one of the tallest office buildings in South America.

facts.fact: A 1973 fire spread from the 14th to the 37th floor and burned for over 12 hours.
facts.quote: The fire rapidly spread from the 14th to the 37th floor and burned for more than 12 hours.

facts.fact: The fire killed four people but did not seriously damage the structure.
facts.quote: The fire left four people dead and 63 injured, but the building did not suffer significant structural damage.

facts.fact: The Figge Art Museum stands on the north bank of the Mississippi in Davenport, Iowa.
facts.quote: The Figge Art Museum is located on the north bank of the Mississippi River in Davenport, Iowa.

facts.fact: Its building, by David Chipperfield, opened on 6 August 2005.
facts.quote: The museum's new building was designed by British architect David Chipperfield and opened to the public August 6, 2005.

facts.fact: It was among Chipperfield's first commissions in the United States.
facts.quote: The Figge was among Chipperfield's first architectural commissions in the United States.

facts.fact: It cost $47 million to build.
facts.quote: The cost of construction was $47 million, $13 million of which was donated by the V.O. and Elizabeth Kahl Figge Foundation.

facts.fact: The museum is 115,000 square feet.
facts.quote: The museum is 115,000 square feet (10,683 m2) and has been accredited by the American Alliance of Museums since 1973.

facts.fact: Its collection of over 4,000 works is best known for Haitian, Colonial Mexican and Midwestern art, including Grant Wood.
facts.quote: The museum has over 4,000 works of art, ranging from the 16th century to the present, and is best known for its extensive collection of Haitian, Colonial Mexican and Midwestern art, particularly pieces by Thomas Hart Benton, Marvin Cone and Grant Wood, including the only self-portrait Wood ever painted.

facts.fact: The Grande Poste is a postal office building on Boulevard Mohamed-Khemisti in central Algiers.
facts.quote: The Algiers Central Post Office, (Arabic: بريد الجزائر المركزي, French: Grande Poste d'Alger) is an office building for postal services located on Boulevard Mohamed-Khemisti, Alger Centre municipality in Algiers, Algeria.

facts.fact: It was designed by Jules Voinot and Marius Toudoire and built in 1910.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Jules Voinot and Marius Toudoire and was constructed in 1910.

facts.fact: It is Algeria's largest post office building.
facts.quote: It is Algeria's largest post office building, In 2015, the state turned it into a museum.

facts.fact: In 2015 the state turned it into a museum.
facts.quote: It is Algeria's largest post office building, In 2015, the state turned it into a museum.

facts.fact: Toudoire, its co-architect, also built major French railway stations, including the Gare de Lyon in Paris.
facts.quote: In particular, he built stations for the Compagnie des chemins de fer de Paris à Lyon et à la Méditerranée (PLM), including the main stations: Paris Lyon to Paris, Bordeaux-Saint-Jean and Toulouse-Matabiau.

facts.fact: The Guaranty Building is an early skyscraper in Buffalo by Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler, completed in 1896.
facts.quote: It was designed by Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler and completed in 1896.

facts.fact: It has 13 floors and stands 167 feet high.
facts.quote: The 13-floor building, 167 feet (51 m) high, was the idea of Buffalonian businessman and entrepreneur Hascal T. Taylor.

facts.fact: Above the lower floors the plan is a U, so every office gets light and fresh air.
facts.quote: Like many Chicago School of architecture buildings, the Guaranty building is a U-shaped plan above the lower levels so that each office could have light and fresh air.

facts.fact: Sullivan based the design on his belief that 'form follows function'.
facts.quote: Sullivan's design for the building was based on his belief that "form follows function".

facts.fact: The steel frame is clad in terracotta blocks, with different blocks marking the three visible zones.
facts.quote: The supporting steel structure of the building was embellished with terra cotta blocks. Different styles of block delineated the three visible zones of the building.

facts.fact: Sullivan gave it a rich programme of floral terracotta ornament.
facts.quote: Although Sullivan told his fellow architects that "we should refrain entirely from the use of ornament for a period of years," he paradoxically gave the Guaranty building a rich program of floral terracotta ornament.

facts.fact: Lifts and stairs were enclosed by metal cages rather than walls, to let light into the halls.
facts.quote: The elevators and staircases were enclosed not by walls, but metal cages permitting light into the hallways.

facts.fact: It became a National Historic Landmark in 1975.
facts.quote: The building was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1975.

facts.fact: Gyumri station is the oldest railway station in Armenia and the city's main station.
facts.quote: Gyumri railway station (Armenian: Գյումրու Երկաթուղային Կայարան), is the oldest railway station in Armenia and the main station of the city of Gyumri.

facts.fact: The Gyumri railway junction, Armenia's oldest and largest, was formed in 1897.
facts.quote: The railway junction of Gyumri is the oldest and the largest one in Armenia. It was formed in 1897.

facts.fact: The present building of 1979 was designed by local architect Rafik Yeghoyan, its entrance hall echoing medieval Armenian architecture.
facts.quote: The present building of the station, built in 1979, was designed by local architect Rafik Yeghoyan, and in some of its features, particularly in the spatial composition of its entrance hall, echoes medieval Armenian architecture, a tendency sometimes characteristic of soviet Armenian modernist architecture.

facts.fact: Trains run from it to Yerevan, Tbilisi and Batumi.
facts.quote: As of 2018, the Gyumri railway station operates regular trips to Yerevan, Tbilisi and Batumi.

facts.fact: The Astrodome in Houston is the world's first multi-purpose domed sports stadium.
facts.quote: The Houston Astrodome, officially the Reliant Astrodome and known simply as the Astrodome, is the world's first multi-purpose, domed sports stadium, located in Houston, Texas, United States.

facts.fact: A covered stadium was thought essential because of Houston's hot, humid, rainy summers.
facts.quote: It was thought a covered stadium was a must for a major league team to be viable in Houston due to the area's subtropical climate and hot summers.

facts.fact: It was designed by Hermon Lloyd & W. B. Morgan with Wilson, Morris, Crain and Anderson; Walter P Moore were the structural engineers.
facts.quote: The Astrodome was designed by architects Hermon Lloyd & W. B. Morgan, and Wilson, Morris, Crain and Anderson (Morris Architects). Structural engineering and structural design were performed by Walter P Moore Engineers and Consultants of Houston.

facts.fact: The dome is 710 feet across; its ceiling is 208 feet above a field sunk 25 feet below street level.
facts.quote: The dome is 710 feet (220 m) in diameter and the ceiling is 208 feet (63 m) above the playing surface, which itself sits 25 feet (7.6 m) below street level.

facts.fact: The nearly circular stadium had movable lower seating so it could host both football and baseball.
facts.quote: The multi-purpose stadium, designed to facilitate both football and baseball, is nearly circular and uses movable lower seating areas.

facts.fact: After the grass died, it became the first major venue to install artificial turf, in 1966, known as AstroTurf.
facts.quote: After the original natural grass playing surface died, the Astrodome became the first major sports venue to install artificial turf in 1966, which became known as AstroTurf.

facts.fact: It led the way for other fully domed stadiums such as the Superdome in New Orleans.
facts.quote: It also ushered in the era of other fully domed stadiums, such as the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, as well as the all now-demolished Pontiac Silverdome near Detroit, Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome in Minneapolis, Kingdome in Seattle, and RCA Dome in Indianapolis.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2014, preventing full demolition.
facts.quote: In 2014, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preventing full demolition as a result.

facts.fact: It is the largest health facility in Kaédi, southern Mauritania, known for its innovative architecture.
facts.quote: The Kaedi Regional Hospital is the largest health facility in Kaédi, in the Gorgol Region in southern Mauritania, and one known for its innovative architecture.

facts.fact: It is built of hand-fired local brick, as a sequence of simple and complex domes.
facts.quote: The hospital involves the use of hand fired locally made brick and a design based on a sequence of simple and complex dome structures.

facts.fact: The building was meant to stay naturally cool while letting in plenty of daylight.
facts.quote: The structure was intended to be both to be naturally cool even while letting in significant light from the outdoors.

facts.fact: It was designed by the Italian architect Fabrizio Carola of ADAUA.
facts.quote: The hospital was designed by the Italian architect Fabrizio Carola of the Association for the Development of Traditional African Urbanism and Architecture (ADAUA).

facts.fact: ADAUA used the project to develop a new 'urban vernacular' and train workers in low-cost local building techniques.
facts.quote: ADAUA  used the design and construction project to develop and disseminate both a new "urban vernacular" architecture for the region and to train workers in new, low-cost and locally appropriate techniques in construction.

facts.fact: Workmen were trained on site.
facts.quote: Workmen were trained on site in the new techniques.

facts.fact: It won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1995.
facts.quote: The hospital won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1995.

facts.fact: Museo Madre is a contemporary art museum in Naples.
facts.quote: The Museo d'Arte Contemporanea Donnaregina, often known as Museo Madre, or Donnaregina Contemporary Art Museum, is a museum of contemporary art in Naples, in Campania in southern Italy.

facts.fact: It occupies the Palazzo Donnaregina, adapted for it by Álvaro Siza.
facts.quote: It is housed in the Palazzo Donnaregina, which was adapted for it by the Portuguese architect Álvaro Siza Vieira.

facts.fact: The museum opened in 2005.
facts.quote: The museum opened in 2005.

facts.fact: It is spread over four floors of the palace, with Mimmo Paladino's sculpture Cavallo on the roof terrace.
facts.quote: The museum is organised on four floors of the palace;| on the roof terrace is Cavallo, a sculpture by Mimmo Paladino which the museum bought in 2007.

facts.fact: The church of Santa Maria Donnaregina Vecchia is entered through the museum.
facts.quote: Access to the church of Santa Maria Donnaregina Vecchia is through the museum.
